opening.headline: When you want to entrust your research, analysis, and report writing to the task at hand, we cover web search, in-depth research, data analysis, and what each agent can do, and to what extent.
body: 'Research the trends of three competitors, analyze sales files, and even create a report.' Web research, file analysis, and report creation all in one request. The menu is lined with names like Web Search, Deep Research, Research, agent, data analysis, and Work. Although the names seem similar, the tasks, time taken, and cost are different.

In this class, we will look at the landscape of functions starting from the lightest web search, to in-depth research that repeatedly explores multiple sources, to data analysis that counts uploaded files, and to agents and work that even entrust execution. Next, we establish criteria to distinguish between questions that are sufficient for general search and those that require research, and explain with examples how to divide the initial one-sentence request into pieces by function.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain differences in agent, in-depth research, search, and data analysis capabilities
Can distinguish between functions that suit business needs and their limitations
The principle of the tool call loop can explain the differences between web search, research, data analysis, and agents.

screens.title: I want to entrust the investigation and analysis to you all at once.
screens.lead: This is a request that contains several things in one sentence. Read the scene below and think about how you can break up the request to reveal the right functionality.

visual.alt: A scene showing one long request sentence and function name chips scattered beneath it.
labels: Research trends of 3 competitors, analyze sales files, and even report

paragraphs: A team leader asked AI this: 'Research the trends of three competitors, analyze sales files, and even create a report.' It's one sentence, but it's three different things happening within it. This involves conducting research by finding and reading various materials on the web, analyzing calculations using uploaded files, and writing reports that organize the results in documents.

When you open the menu of the AI app, you will find names such as Web Search, Deep Research, Research, agent, data analysis, and Work. When you look at the names, they all seem like 'automatic search functions', but they do different things. There are functions that end with one or two searches, there are functions that read dozens of sources in a matter of minutes, there are functions that compute files into code and functions that execute multiple steps on your behalf.
The question for this class is this. What function does what, and to what extent? When you break the request into parts, you start to see the functionality you need.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Would it be easier to review the results: entrusting everything to one function that appears to be the most powerful, or dividing the functions according to the nature of the work?

screens.outro: Now that you have the sense to share your requests, let's think about the tasks you have been tasked with.

screens.title: Thinking about what I have been entrusted with
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think for yourself first and then click.

items.prompt: Have you ever asked AI to ‘search and organize things’ and the result was shallow?
items.answer: A regular web search is a function that produces answers in one or two tool calls. Tool calling is when the model calls a tool such as search, and the principle is explained in the next screen. It's quick and good for checking facts, but it can feel shallow on topics that require comparing multiple sources. That's when it's time to write in-depth research.

items.prompt: Have you ever used a survey feature that required waiting several minutes?
items.answer: Claude's Research is indicated as being suitable for comprehensive investigations that take 1 to 3 minutes over five tool calls, while in-depth investigations with Perplexity and Gemini also take several minutes. Waiting time is the time spent in iterative search. It's important to first decide whether the question is worth waiting for.

items.prompt: Have you ever uploaded an Excel file and entrusted it with calculations or charts?
items.answer: Data analysis functions code files to create tables and charts. The quality of the results largely depends on the structure of the file, so in this lesson we'll directly compare the differences between good and bad sheets.

screens.outro: Let's start with the lightest feature: web browsing.

screens.title: Tool calls and agent loops
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn how models use tools and where they differ from web searches to agents. The final tab covers reasons why things can be wrong even if they have good evidence.

visual.alt: A loop diagram in which the model requests a tool call, the product executes it, and returns the result.
labels: Model: Think and Request a Call
Write your answer if you have enough

tabs.label: What is a tool call?
tabs.body:
Language models only read text and write text. This is how things like browsing the web or running code are done. When the model sends text requesting 'search for this term', the product actually runs the tool and passes the results back to the model. One part of this process of requesting, executing, and delivering results is a tool call.

Therefore, the model does not directly access the Internet or open files. The product and settings determine which tools can be used and to what extent they can be implemented.

tabs.label: Loop: think, call, observe
tabs.body:
After receiving the results, the model reads them and determines whether they are sufficient. If it's not enough, call it again with a different search term, and if it's enough, write an answer. This iteration is the agent loop.

Yao et al.'s ReAct study proposed a method in which the model makes inferences and actions alternately, receives the results of the actions as external information, and uses them for the next inference. Anthropic's agent design guide also describes the agent as a loop that uses tools based on results received from the environment, and recommends having an exit condition such as a maximum number of iterations and a human confirmation point.

tabs.label: The number of calls is time consuming and burdensome for review.
tabs.body:
Each time a call occurs, execution time and usage are consumed, and the received results accumulate, increasing the amount of data read by the model. The reason in-depth research takes several minutes is because we make dozens of these calls.

As the number of calls increases, so does the number of sources and intermediate judgments that must be reviewed by humans. So running a long loop on a question that only takes one or two calls will only cost you time, money, and increase the number of things to review. The first criterion for feature selection is the habit of first estimating the number of calls required for a question.

tabs.label: The difference in functionality is the length of the loop and the tools allowed
tabs.body:
The functionality covered in this lesson builds on the same loop principle. Searching the web is a short loop that uses the search tool once or twice. Data analysis is a loop that uses a code execution tool to build code, then view and modify the execution results. In-depth research is a long loop of planning, searching, and reading that is compiled into a report. The agent is a long loop that even allows tools to manipulate the site or app you're logged into.

In other words, the difference lies in how long the loop runs and what tools it allows. The more permissions a tool has to write or manipulate an app, the more important permissions and verification procedures become.

tabs.label: Why it can be wrong even if there is evidence
tabs.body:
At the end of the loop, the model reads the results it received, summarizes them, and writes an answer. During this summarization step, the model can plausibly invent content that is not in the original text or misrepresent content from the source. This phenomenon is called hallucination, and it is a long-studied problem in the field of language production.

Citations only indicate the source and do not guarantee that the summary matches the original text. So numbers, dates, and key arguments should be checked directly against the original text by opening the citation.

screens.outro: Now that we know the principle of loops, let's look at the shortest loop, web search.

screens.title: Web searches and light research
screens.lead: Select the arrows to move through each step and follow the flow of web search answering your questions and how to check them.

steps.title: A question comes in
steps.body: Web search is the lightest feature for questions that require up-to-date information or sources. ChatGPT web search answers with links to relevant sources and even turns on automatically when questions require it. To turn it on directly, select Search from the Tools menu or start by entering a slash in the input field.

steps.title: Search is performed
steps.body: The model searches the web with search terms that match your question and reads the results. Claude Web Search also pulls real-time information on supported models, and in Team and Enterprise, the owner must first turn it on in the workspace. The model's learning knowledge has a base date, and this function is the easiest way to compensate for this limitation.

steps.title: Answers and citations are displayed
steps.body: The result is an answer with quotations attached. Claude explains that if you do a web search, all responses will be cited. The presence of a citation means that the source can be verified, but is not a guarantee that the content is correct.

steps.title: Open the source and check
steps.body: Click on the quote in the response to open the original text and check whether the answer matches the original text. For content that would be difficult to find if incorrect, such as numbers or dates, read the original text. It is up to the user to check.

steps.title: A web search is the right question
steps.body: The Claude article explains that web searches are best suited for simple fact-checking that can be answered with one or two tool calls. Questions such as today's weather, information about a specific company, recent news headlines, or yesterday's game results. We also note that web search is a different function than sidebar search for finding saved chats and projects.

screens.outro: Now that you know the light search, let's take a look at the deep investigation features.

screens.title: In-Depth Research: Breaking Down Questions, Sources, Reports
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare how the three products' in-depth investigation capabilities handle planning, sources, and reports. The final tab organizes common structures.

visual.alt: A diagram of in-depth research output organized into three sections: research plan, source discovery, and report.
labels: Possible to stop or adjust during progress

tabs.label: ChatGPT
tabs.body:
ChatGPT's Deep research suggests a research plan when you tell it your desired results, and lets you review and revise that plan before you start. You can stop along the way and adjust the direction or source you want to approach.

The output is a structured report with citations and links. You will be notified that the default sources are the public web, uploaded files, and connected apps, and that connected apps only use read operations and do not use write operations.

Therefore, there is relatively little worry about changes to sensitive data while entrusting the investigation. However, since information is input to AI even by reading, you need to check which app is connected.

tabs.label: Gemini
tabs.body:
Gemini's Deep Research is your personal research assistant in four steps: planning, searching, inferring, and reporting. It is said to explore hundreds of sites and create multi-page reports in minutes.

The app help contains separate information on how to use Deep Research in the Gemini app, and available accounts and settings can be found in the app help. The result has the same structure. Research plan, sources explored, and synthesized report.

It is helpful to understand that the steps are identified by name. Questions are broken down in the planning phase, data is gathered in the search phase, data are compared in the inference phase, and documents are created in the reporting phase.

tabs.label: Claude
tabs.body:
Claude's Research is a function that synthesizes information from services connected to the web. The help explains that it is suitable for comprehensive information gathering, requiring five or more tool invocations and taking between one and three minutes. Examples include comparing competitors or updating old internal documents with web information.

It is like any other product in that it synthesizes multiple sources to create a report with citations. It is better to use only expanded thinking for tasks that require complex reasoning but do not require up-to-date web information, and by using the two together, you can do both approach planning and extensive collection.

tabs.label: common structure
tabs.body:
The output of the three products can be read in the same three compartments. The first is planning, breaking down the question into sub-questions. The second is sources, which collects data from the public web, files, and connected services. The third is a report, which is compiled with citations.

All three products take a few minutes to produce results, and that time is spent on iterative searches. Since there are many sources, not all of the content is accurate, so it is still necessary to open and check the citations. Additionally, the habit of reviewing your plan before you start will reduce wasted effort.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the research features, let's look at the data analysis features.

screens.title: Data Analysis Features: File Structure Determines Results
screens.lead: Below is an example of a good and bad sheet side by side. By selecting the underlined passages, you can see which rules lead to better data analysis results and why.

visual.alt: A flowchart in which the uploaded file goes through code execution and becomes a table and chart.
labels: Tables and charts, assumptions and interpretation explanations

data.text:
Good sheet (Revenue_2026)  
Region | month | Product | sales  
Seoul | January | A | 1200000  
Seoul | January | B | 800,000  
Busan | January | A | 650,000  

Poor sheet  
(first row is empty)  
Revenue Status / Total / Remarks / Notes  
Inventory table is attached below one regional table.

marks.note: The first row contains descriptive column names. Data analysis looks at column names to determine what each column means, so having names in the first row makes calculations and groupings accurate. Even in tidy data, which is a widely used organizing principle in the field of statistics, variables are placed in columns and observations are placed in rows.

Each row contains one record. Region, month, and product describe one sale per line. Only with this structure can calculations that total by region or product be performed reliably using code. If the model mentally calculates large sums as if they were writing letters together, it can be wrong, so this function runs the code to calculate it, and the model explains the code and results. The code produces the same results for the same input, making it easy for humans to verify.
It's a problem of bad sheets. If the first row is empty, you may not find the column names, or you may read the wrong line as the name.

marks.span: Inventory table is attached below one regional table.
marks.note: The problem is mixing unrelated tables on one sheet. The structures of the two tables are different, so if the code tries to read them as one table, the calculations will be incorrect. Organize the sheets by dividing them into tables. Following the same principle, tables with different observation targets are kept as separate tables.

screens.outro: Now that we know the analysis, let’s look at the class of agents who are entrusted with the work.

ext.title: Tidy Data (Hadley Wickham, Journal of Statistical Software)

screens.title: Agent and Work, Workspace Agent, Codex
screens.lead: By selecting the numbered markers above the picture, you can see the lineage leading from interactive functions to functions that are left to execution, as well as the points of note for each function.

visual.alt: A functional tree that starts from Chat and branches out to agent, work, workspace agent, and Codex.

markers.label: agent method
markers.title: When you tell a task, it starts executing it.
markers.body:
The basic form of agent methods is that you describe a task and the agent starts executing it, stops and asks for confirmation if it needs confirmation, and can change direction or stop mid-task.

Using the site or app you're logged in to can access your sensitive data. Therefore, the risk of prompt injection, an attack where hidden sentences in a web page or document are about to be read to change the model's behavior, and the verification process before high-impact tasks are important. In ChatGPT, long, multi-step tasks are taken over by the Work of the next marker.

markers.label: Work
markers.title: Long, multi-step tasks and finished results
markers.body:
ChatGPT consists of Chat and Work. Chat is for quick conversations and casual questions, while Work is an agent designed for longer, multi-step tasks and finished deliverables. Usage follows the same structure as Codex.

Therefore, Work is the right candidate for jobs that involve research, analysis, and document writing, as in the first request. However, since it takes a long time and requires a lot of usage, Chat is suitable for simple questions.

markers.label: Workspace Agent
markers.title: Organizations perform repetitive tasks as agents
markers.body:
Business and Enterprise allow you to create repeatable tasks as agents. Test before publishing, pick models and inference strengths, connect apps and tools, share with teammates or workspaces, write in Slack, run on schedule, or launch with API.

It is turned off by default in Enterprise workspaces and must be turned on by an administrator, and role-based access control ensures that users can only see and run agents they have permission to access.

markers.label: Codex
markers.title: For software development only
markers.body:
Codex is a function dedicated to software development and technical work. You can use it in the desktop app, and with Codex Cloud, you can start and continue coding on desktop, web, and mobile.

If your purpose is research or document writing, it is better to choose Chat or Work rather than Codex. The habit of choosing by the nature of the task rather than by the name of the function is the key to this genealogy.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the functional landscape, let's practice our selection criteria with an example.

screens.title: Case Commentary 1: Questions that are sufficient for general search and require research
screens.lead: The instructor categorizes the four questions into three criteria. Select the arrows and follow the steps as standards and judgments are added one by one.

steps.title: four questions
steps.body: There are four questions to categorize. ‘What is the exchange rate today?’, ‘What was yesterday’s economic result?’, ‘Comparison of the three competitors’ strategies and market reactions over the past year’, and ‘Updating the internal pricing policy document with the latest market data.’

steps.title: Criteria 1: How many tool calls are needed?
steps.body: Exchange rates and match results are just a search or two away. Comparing competitor strategies requires five or more calls because multiple sources for each company must be located and compared. The number of calls is what distinguishes Claude documents from web searches and research.

steps.title: Criterion 2: What is the outcome?
steps.body: A one-line answer about exchange rates is enough. Competitor comparisons can only be used in decision-making if there is a report with sources. Ask whether the output will look like a one-line answer or a report with citations.

steps.title: Criterion 3: Should source scope be directly controlled?
steps.body: ChatGPT Deep research allows you to review your plan before you start and adjust the sources you will access along the way. Research is a good fit if you need to control the scope of both the public web and internal materials, such as updating internal documents.

steps.title: Classification results
steps.body: ‘What is the exchange rate today?’ and ‘What was yesterday’s match result?’ are web searches. ‘Comparing three competitors’ and ‘updating internal documents’ are research. If you use research for simple checks, you'll wait a few minutes and spend more money, and if you use web searches for comprehensive research, you'll get shallow answers.

screens.outro: Now that we've established a baseline, let's break down the initial one-sentence request by function.

screens.title: Case commentary 2: Divide the initial request by function
screens.lead: Selecting the three pieces from the initial request will unlock the appropriate features and precautions. First, decide for yourself which function is right for you and then press it.

items.answer: This is research. You can iteratively explore multiple sources to get a report with provenance. If necessary, you can include connected apps like Drive or Mail as read-only. Review your research plan before you begin, and open the citation after you're done to check key figures.

Data analysis. Put descriptive column names in the first row of the file, one record per row, and organize unrelated tables by dividing them into sheets. You then specify which calculations, groupings, and charts to create based on which columns. Since the analysis is supported by code, we also read the assumptions and interpretation of the results.

This is the step of turning the results into documents. Long, multi-step tasks and completed results are the domain of ChatGPT Work, while editing functions such as Canvas are suitable for just refining a draft. The results of the previous two steps are passed as input to be organized according to the report frame.

items.prompt: What are the limitations to watch out for?
items.answer: App connections and agents touch sensitive data. So we start with a focus on reading, and leave a confirmation phase for writing operations. The bottom line is to divide the work by function rather than handing it over all at once, and have a person review the results of each step before moving on to the next step.

screens.outro: Now that we have finished explaining the case, we will summarize the main points of this lesson.

screens.title: Divide requests and select features
screens.lead: Let's organize the topography of the functions covered in this class by connecting it to the first question.

paragraphs: The initial question was which function does what and to what extent. Web searches are written in questions that end in one or two searches, and are answered with citations. These functions are all loops where the model repeats tool calls, the difference lies in the length of the loop and the tools allowed. Deep Research and Research creates a plan and iterative exploration of multiple sources to produce a report with citations. Data analysis creates tables and charts by calculating structured files with code. A family of agents executes multiple steps, and in ChatGPT, long, multi-step tasks are taken over by Work.

There are three criteria for selecting features. How many tool calls are needed, whether the output is a one-line answer or a report, and whether you have direct control over the scope of the sources. Choose by the nature of the work, not by the name of the function.

Break down one large request into pieces such as research, analysis, and documentation. The results of each step are reviewed by a human, the citation is opened and confirmed, and app connection or execution functions have a confirmation process that starts with a reading focus.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: When you receive a request, first count how many pieces it is divided into and choose the appropriate function for each piece.

checks.q: What's the best reason why in-depth research functions take so much longer than regular web searches?
options: This is because the model writes down the answer more slowly.
This is because it runs a loop that repeats calling the tool and reading the results several times.
This is because search results are first checked by human reviewers.
This is because the model connects directly to the Internet to attach quotations.
checks.explain: A tool call is a cycle where the model requests a call and the product executes and returns a result, and research repeats this cycle for a long time. The number of calls equals time, money, and review burden.

wrong.0: The time is determined by the number of times the call is repeated, not by the speed of writing.
wrong.2: This is not the time it takes for a person to check in the middle.
wrong.3: The product executes the tool rather than the model connecting directly.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: I had the data analyzed using the uploaded Excel file, but the results were a mess. The file has an empty first row and contains several unrelated tables mixed together on one sheet. What is the most appropriate prescription?
options: Switch to Deep Research to explore more sources
Switch to ChatGPT agent and process it directly on the site you are logged in to.
Put descriptive column names in the first row, organize the table with one record per row, and divide the table into sheets.
Shorten analysis requests and let the model make decisions on its own
checks.explain: Data analysis works well with well-structured files. Column names, rows and records, and table separation are important, and it is more accurate to specify calculations, groups, and charts.

wrong.0: Research is a function for exploring sources, so it does not solve file structure problems.
wrong.1: Agents run the risk of touching sensitive data and are not a solution to file structure issues.
wrong.3: To be more accurate, you need to specify which columns, calculations, and charts to use.

options: Web search. Because one or two searches is enough.
Research. This is because a report with provenance is needed by repeatedly searching multiple sources.
Data analysis. This is because tables and charts are the key to comparison.
agent. This is because it involves manipulating the site you logged in to.
checks.explain: Research is a job that requires a lot of tool calls and the results must be reports with sources. A regular search is faster for simple checks.

wrong.0: This request is broad in scope, suitable for questions that end with one or two searches.
wrong.2: There is no need to calculate or chart uploaded data.

glossary.def: This is a function that retrieves real-time web information and responds with a source link. This is suitable for questions that require one or two searches.
This function creates a research plan, explores multiple sources, and creates a report with citations.
This function creates tables and charts by calculating uploaded data with code.
A feature that executes multiple steps on behalf of the user and asks for confirmation when needed.
This is a function that allows organizations to create repetitive tasks as agents, share them, and schedule and execute them.
When the model requests the use of a tool like search or code execution, the product executes it and returns the results. Repeating this is the agent loop.

misconceptions.myth: Deep Research is always better than regular search.
misconceptions.fact: For simple fact-checking, a regular web search is faster and sufficient. Research is suitable for comprehensive investigations that require repeated exploration of multiple sources.

misconceptions.myth: There is no need to check the research results as they depend on the source.
misconceptions.fact: Citations are just a way to verify. As the model may be translated differently from the original text in the process of summarizing the content of the source, key figures and claims should be opened in citations to check if they are consistent with the original text.

misconceptions.myth: Agents work safely on their own.
misconceptions.fact: When you use a site or app you are logged in to, there is a risk of reaching sensitive data and prompt injection, where hidden sentences in the read content change the model's behavior. High-impact work requires verification procedures.

misconceptions.myth: The model executes searches or code directly.
misconceptions.fact: The model simply issues text requesting a tool call, and the actual execution is handled by the product and returns the results to the model. The product and settings determine which tools can be used.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Web searches and in-depth research are chosen based on the depth of the question.
Data analysis creates calculations and charts from structured files.
Since the agent series is entrusted with execution, authority and confirmation procedures are important.
Each request is divided into functions and the results are reviewed step by step.
